How reading works

Source: vignettes/reading.Rmd
reading.Rmd
library(crate)

What crate knows about

Every file or table crate knows about is a row in its registry, keyed by a source family and a file name. A file entry is one crate reads and normalizes with crt_ingest(). A schema_only entry declares a canonical shape for data crate does not read, which you hold to that shape yourself with crt_schema_conform().

crt_files()
#> # A tibble: 14 × 6
#>    source file_name                  kind  handler_fn schema_yaml canonical_cols
#>    <chr>  <chr>                      <chr> <chr>      <chr>       <chr>         
#>  1 bcfp   user_habitat_classificati… file  crt_handl… schemas/bc… blue_line_key…
#>  2 nge    track_sessions             sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,sessi…
#>  3 nge    track_vertices             sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,sessi…
#>  4 nge    track_annotations          sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,sessi…
#>  5 nge    form_capture               sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,form,…
#>  6 nge    discharge/fwa/v1/segment_… sche… NA         schemas/ng… linear_featur…
#>  7 nge    discharge/fwa/v1/segment_… sche… NA         schemas/ng… linear_featur…
#>  8 nge    discharge/fwa/v1/watershe… sche… NA         schemas/ng… watershed_fea…
#>  9 nge    form_pscis                 sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,form,…
#> 10 nge    form_fiss_site             sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,form,…

#> 13 nge    form_monitoring            sche… NA         schemas/ng… project,form,…
#> 14 nge    fish_data                  file  crt_handl… schemas/ng… local_name,sp…

One call, either shape

bcfishpass changed user_habitat_classification.csv on 2026-04-26 from a long format, one row per segment, species and habitat type with a text habitat_ind of "t" or "f", to a wide format with integer spawning and rearing columns. crate ships a small fixture of each:

long_path <- system.file(
  "extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_long.csv",
  package = "crate"
)
wide_path <- system.file(
  "extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_wide.csv",
  package = "crate"
)
names(readr::read_csv(long_path, show_col_types = FALSE))
#>  [1] "blue_line_key"            "downstream_route_measure"
#>  [3] "upstream_route_measure"   "watershed_group_code"    
#>  [5] "species_code"             "habitat_type"            
#>  [7] "habitat_ind"              "reviewer_name"           
#>  [9] "review_date"              "source"                  
#> [11] "notes"
names(readr::read_csv(wide_path, show_col_types = FALSE))
#>  [1] "blue_line_key"            "downstream_route_measure"
#>  [3] "upstream_route_measure"   "watershed_group_code"    
#>  [5] "species_code"             "spawning"                
#>  [7] "rearing"                  "reviewer_name"           
#>  [9] "review_date"              "source"                  
#> [11] "notes"

The same call reads both to the canonical wide shape:

long <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", long_path)
wide <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", wide_path)
identical(names(long), names(wide))
#> [1] TRUE
str(long[c("spawning", "rearing")])
#> tibble [5 × 2] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>  $ spawning: int [1:5] 1 NA 1 NA 1
#>  $ rearing : int [1:5] 1 1 NA 1 1

Five pieces at runtime

When you call crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", path), five pieces wire together:

  1. Registry (inst/extdata/crate_registry.csv) maps each (source, file_name) pair to its kind, its schema YAML and, for a file entry, its handler function. It is what crt_files() prints above.
  2. Schema YAML (inst/extdata/schemas/bcfp/user_habitat_classification.yaml) declares the canonical columns (names, types, required flags) and each known upstream variant: a set of column names and an id. crt_schema_read() loads it.
  3. Handler (R/crt_handler_bcfp_user_habitat_classification.R), one function per file entry. crate matches the file’s column names against each variant’s (the first set-equal match wins) and passes the matched variant’s id to the handler. Here 2026-04-26-wide passes the data through, and pre-2026-04-26-long pivots the long rows to wide, turning the habitat_ind text into integer indicators in the same step.
  4. Validation (crt_schema_validate()) checks that every column the schema declares required: true is present, and fails listing all that are missing.
  5. Type enforcement (crt_schema_apply()) coerces each declared column the data has to its schema type (integer, double, string, logical or datetime). Whatever types a handler returns, the schema’s are the ones that come out, and readr’s guesses (a double for an integer column, a Date for a declared string) do not leak through.

Steps 4 and 5 are crt_schema_conform(), which crt_ingest() calls rather than repeats, so a file crate reads and a data frame you bring get the same treatment. The handler, crt_schema_read(), crt_schema_validate() and crt_schema_apply() are internal: you call crt_ingest() or crt_schema_conform(), and they call the rest.

A datetime is an instant

A datetime column is an instant, and crate never moves it. A POSIXct has its timezone attribute stamped to UTC rather than converted. Several readers return correct UTC instants with no timezone label, which R then renders in the session’s zone, so they read as a clock in another timezone. Converting them to “fix” that rendering would put a whole-hour error into every join downstream. Stamping fixes the label, which was the only thing wrong.

Variant matching uses column names only

crt_ingest() picks the upstream variant by the set of column names alone. It does not compare column types at that step, so an upstream file that kept its column names and changed a type would reach the handler misshapen. crt_schema_apply() then coerces the output, and some coercions turn a value into NA without an error (as.integer("yes")). Checking types at dispatch is crate#55.

Required columns and output types are still enforced, by steps 4 and 5.

Registering a file or table

How to add a (source, file_name) pair, a schema, a registry row, a handler for a file entry, a decision entry and tests with fixtures, is in inst/extdata/schemas/README.md.
